measurement: secrets-exposure false alarms on real code. The 16-pattern shipped path (regex-only, FIXOR_SECRETS_LLM_OPT_IN unset) rerun keyless over the 13 step-4 clones on disk with the step-4 harness unchanged; every flag read blind by three independent readers; every grounds sentence audited. Counts with denominators, never a rate.

The detector's own path filter (test/tests/__tests__/spec/fixtures/examples/scripts/dev-tools/migrations/seed/demo) and server-only marker skip files AFTER they are counted; the denominator is files scanned, not files matched.

secondWay.rule: R12: before believing a number, ask the same question a second way. A separate script with the same walker rules and synthetic diff builder called ONLY SecretsExposureDetector.detect() under the same lock and counted its throws by itself.

reading.protocol: HANDOFF.md blind reading protocol, flag form: fresh subagents, batches of at most 56 (30 and 20 used), permitted to read only docs/detector-capabilities.md and the packet files; never detector source, fixtures, scripts; never told the repository, selector or arm. Each packet: relative path inside the clone, flagged line number, the flagged line marked >>>, 20 lines of context each side. Answer 'real credential' or 'not a credential' with one grounds sentence that states what the value is, without reproducing it.

readers.lensB: adversarial reader instructed to establish that the line IS a real credential and to answer 'real credential' whenever the packet cannot rule it out, 2 batches of 30
readers.audit: 3 auditors of 20 packets each; for every (packet, lens) grounds sentence: does it state a fact visible in the packet about what the value is, and does that fact by itself make the verdict

readerControlsR12.rule: The reader is an instrument. Two planted packets, indistinguishable in form from the flags, were interleaved at seeded positions: a positive (a hardcoded sk_live_ literal in a production billing client, value randomly generated, never issued anywhere) that a working reader must call 'real credential', and a negative (a documented placeholder password in a defaults file, rejected by a validator in the same packet) that a working reader must call 'not a credential'. Excluded from every count.

A.grounds: The value is a your-password-here style placeholder that the adjacent validateConfig function explicitly rejects with an error demanding the real value from the environment.

B.grounds: The value is a self-describing placeholder phrase telling the reader to put their password here, which the adjacent validateConfig() function explicitly rejects with a must-be-set error.

C.grounds: The value is a hyphenated '[VALUE:18 chars]' placeholder phrase in a defaults object, and the adjacent comment plus validateConfig function explicitly reject that exact placeholder at startup.

A.note: "[VALUE:18 chars]" rejected by validateConfig throwing '[VALUE:23 chars]'.

B.note: "[VALUE:18 chars]" rejected by validateConfig throwing '[VALUE:23 chars]'.

C.note: Comment on line 8 and validateConfig on lines 14-18 both visible.

results.controlKind: placeholder value in a default config

A.grounds: The value is a live-mode Stripe secret key literal (sk_live prefix followed by a random-looking token) passed directly to the Stripe client constructor in production billing code.

B.grounds: The value is a Stripe live-mode secret key literal (sk_live_ prefix followed by a random-looking body) passed directly into the Stripe client constructor of production billing code, with nothing in the packet marking it as an example.

C.grounds: The value is a live-mode Stripe secret key literal (sk_live prefix followed by a random-looking token) passed straight into the Stripe client constructor in the production billing module, with nothing in the packet marking it as a placeholder.

A.note: sk_live_ prefix, random 24-char body, passed straight to new Stripe() in src/billing/stripe.ts used by checkout/invoice routes.

B.note: Matches packet; no placeholder marker anywhere in the 20 lines.

results.controlKind: hardcoded live key in production source
